_comment: Two read-only captures from controlplane.tailscale.com. The 2026-08-01 ECDSA capture is retained as a regression fixture. On 2026-08-12 the endpoint required an RSA-PSS offer and selected the Generation Y RSA chain recorded below. Let's Encrypt can reissue, so tests validate the committed public chains rather than assuming either selection forever.
provenance: openssl s_client with ECDSA+SHA256 only; leaf recovered from Cert Spotter issuance 15207156327 and static CAs from Let's Encrypt

key_exchange._comment: The IPv4 and IPv6 frontends differ. Measured against four fixed IPv4 backends, X25519-only was refused 8/8 while P-256-only succeeded 8/8; over IPv6 X25519-only succeeded 3/3. embedded-tls offers Secp256r1 (P-256), so the IPv4 route works — but a client that offered only X25519 would fail on IPv4 and succeed on IPv6, which is exactly the kind of difference that reads as an intermittent bug.
